He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]]. ==Early life== Cockburn was born in [[Kingston, Jamaica]], and in 2014, moved to [[Queens]], [[New York (state)|New York]], to be with his mother, who had moved to Queens in 2009.{{cite web | url=https://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/high-school/kofi-cockburn/ | title=From Kingston, Jamaica to Oak Hill: Coffee Cockburn Keeps Climbing | publisher=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] | author=Squadron, Alex | date=21 July 2018 | access-date=7 January 2019}} In addition to his participation in basketball at a young age, Cockburn also played [[soccer]], [[cricket]], and ran in [[track and field]]. ==High school career== Cockburn first enrolled in high school at St. Andrew Technical High in Kingston, Jamaica, then [[Christ the King Regional High School]] in [[Middle Village, New York]].{{cite web |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=6'11 teen left Jamaica for NY — and now has huge hoops potential |url=https://nypost.com/2016/05/28/611-teen-left-jamaica-for-ny-and-now-has-huge-hoops-potential/ |publisher=[[New York Post]] |access-date=7 January 2019 |date=28 May 2016}} He played [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball for the New York (NY) Rens, and was teammates with his future [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] teammate [[Alan Griffin (basketball)|Alan Griffin]].{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Kofi Cockburn talks Illinois visit, future plans |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2018/12/31/kofi-cockburn-talks-illinois-visit-future-plans/ |website=Zagsblog.com |access-date=7 January 2019 |date=31 December 2018}} During the summer of 2018 on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) circuit with the NY Rens, Cockburn averaged 16.3 points and 10.3 rebounds per game, while shooting 53.9 percent from the field.{{cite web |author=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=6 January 2019 |title=Kofi Cockburn chooses Illinois over Pittsburgh, UConn |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25699291 |access-date=7 January 2019 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} Prior to his junior year, Cockburn was selected to participate in the 2017 [[Basketball Without Borders]] Americas camp that was held in [[Nassau, Bahamas]].{{cite web |title=BWB Americas Daily Blog From the Bahamas |url=http://global.nba.com/news/bwb-americas-2017-oficially-tips-off-today/ |publisher=[[Kansas City Star]] |access-date=7 January 2019 |date=5 July 2017}} After his junior season, Cockburn was named to the World Team for the 2018 [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |title=Kofi Cockburn Added to World Team for 2018 Nike Hoop Summit |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2018/04/world-team-cockburn.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190108045701/https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2018/04/world-team-cockburn.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=8 January 2019 |publisher=USA Basketball |access-date=7 January 2019 |date=10 April 2018}} For his senior season, Cockburn transferred to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]], where he was teammates with fellow five-star recruits [[Cole Anthony]] and [[Cam Thomas (basketball)|Cameron Thomas]].{{cite web |title=New York City stars Cole Anthony, Kofi Cockburn transfer to Oak Hill Academy |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/bt3wkTqLvU2KA4ugQPILGA/new-york-city-stars-cole-anthony,-kofi-cockburn-transfer-to-oak-hill-academy.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=7 January 2019 |date=30 July 2018}} ===Recruiting=== Prior to his senior high school season at Oak Hill Academy, Cockburn held 26 scholarship offers and narrowed the list of schools he was considering to 12, which included [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]], [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]], [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] and [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]].{{cite web |title=KU on another list of 12 |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article215957960.html |publisher=[[Kansas City Star]] |access-date=7 January 2019 |date=1 August 2018 | author=Bedore, Gary}} Citing his relationship with Illinois assistant coach [[Orlando Antigua]] and the rest of the Illinois coaching staff, Cockburn committed to playing college basketball for [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] on 6 January 2019.{{cite web |title=Illinois goes big with five-star Kofi Cockburn |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/illinois-goes-big-with-five-star-kofi-cockburn |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=7 January 2019 |date=6 January 2019 | author=Evans, Corey}} Cockburn was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and was considered a top 50 player in the 2019 class.{{cite web |title=Kofi Cockburn |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2019/kofi-cockburn-180529 |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=7 January 2019}}{{cite web |title=Five-star center Cockburn commits to Illinois |url=http://www.news-gazette.com/sports/illini-sports/2019-01-06/five-star-center-cockburn-commits-illinois.html |publisher=[[The News-Gazette (Champaign-Urbana)|The News-Gazette]] |access-date=7 | espn overall = 50 | access-date = 7 January 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== ===2019–20 season=== [[File:Kofi Cockburn Jon Teske.jpg|thumb|Cockburn (right) with [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] in 2020]] In his debut for Illinois, Cockburn had 10 points and 11 rebounds to help defeat [[Nicholls Colonels men's basketball|Nicholls]] 78–70 in overtime.{{cite news |title=Feliz helps Illinois hold off Nicholls State 78–70 in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166016 |access-date=22 November 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=5 November 2019}} The following game, Cockburn scored 23 points and pulled down 14 rebounds in a 83–71 win over [[Grand Canyon Antelopes men's basketball|Grand Canyon]].{{cite news |title=Cockburn leads way as Illinois holds off Grand Canyon 83–71 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169933 |access-date=21 November 2019 |work=ESPN |agency=Associated Press |date=8 November 2019}} Cockburn was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] player of the week on 25 November after setting a school freshman record for rebounds in a game with 17 to go along with 18 points in a win versus [[The Citadel Bulldogs basketball|The Citadel]].{{cite web |url=https://bigten.org/news/2019/11/25/illinois-cockburn-claims-both-weekly-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200408143243/https://bigten.org/news/2019/11/25/illinois-cockburn-claims-both-weekly-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=8 April 2020|title=Illinois' Cockburn Claims Both Weekly Men's Basketball Honors|access-date=26 November 2019 |date=25 November 2019 |website=BigTen.org}} On 11 December 2020, Cockburn had 19 points, 10 rebounds and four blocks in a 71–62 victory over fifth-ranked [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], Illinois' first win over a top-five program since 2013.{{cite news |last1=Medcalf |first1=Myron |title=Illinois' Kofi Cockburn accidentally clobbers official while celebrating bucket |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28280058 |access-date=12 December 2019 |work=ESPN |date=11 December 2019}} At the close of the regular season, Cockburn was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Freshman of the Year. He was selected to the Third Team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] by the media and was Honorable Mention All-Conference according to the coaches.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2020/3/9/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200309231733/https://bigten.org/news/2020/3/9/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 March 2020|title=Big Ten Unveils Men's Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=9 March 2020 |access-date=9 March 2020}} As a freshman, Cockburn was Illinois' second-leading scorer and top rebounder, averaging 13.3 points and 8.8 rebounds per game while leading the Illini with 1.4 blocks per game. He shot 53.2 percent from the floor and 67.7 percent at the foul line. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Richey |first1=Scott |title=Illini center Cockburn declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.news-gazette.com/sports/cockburn-declaring-for-nba-draft/article_3c1deea4-7903-11ea-bb74-bf2886148da0.html |access-date=8 April 2020 |work=[[The News-Gazette]] |date=7 April 2020}} ===2020–21 season=== On August 1, Cockburn announced he was pulling out of the draft and returning for his sophomore season.{{cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=1 August 2020 |title=Kofi Cockburn returning to Illinois for sophomore season |work=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29578713 |access-date=2 August 2020}} As a sophomore, Cockburn averaged 17.7 points, 9.5 rebounds and 1.3 blocks per game, shooting 65.4 percent from the field. He was a Second Team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and First Team All-Big Ten selection. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] and entered the transfer portal. ===2021–22 season=== Cockburn ultimately returned for his junior season at Illinois.{{cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Kofi Cockburn staying with Illinois after entering transfer portal |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31829449 |access-date=1 November 2021 |work=ESPN |date=16 July 2021}} He was suspended for the first three games of his junior season due to selling apparel and memorabilia.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=NCAA suspends Illinois star center Kofi Cockburn 3 games for selling apparel, memorabilia |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32527949 |access-date=1 November 2021 |work=ESPN |date=1 November 2021}} On 26 November 2021, Cockburn scored a career-high 38 points along with 10 rebounds in a 94–85 win against [[UT Rio Grande Valley Vaqueros men's basketball|Texas–Rio Grande Valley]].{{cite news |title=Cockburn's career night lifts No. 14 Illinois to 94–85 win |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401371390 |access-date=27 November 2021 |work=ESPN |agency=Associated Press |date=26 November 2021}} He was named to the First Team All-Big Ten.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308180525/https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=8 March 2022|title=2021-22 Big Ten Men's Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|publisher=Big Ten Conference |date=8 March 2022 |access-date=8 March 2022}} As a junior, Cockburn averaged 20.9 points and 10.6 rebounds per game. On 20 April 2022, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Kofi Cockburn declares for 2022 NBA Draft: Illinois star big man forgoing remaining eligibility to enter pros |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/kofi-cockburn-declares-for-2022-nba-draft-illinois-star-big-man-forgoing-remaining-eligibility-to-enter-pros/ |access-date=20 April 2022 |work=[[CBSSports.com]] |date=20 April 2022}} ==Professional career== Cockburn went undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. He then signed an [[NBA salary cap#Exhibit 10|Exhibit 10 contract]] with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite news |last1=Pontbriand |first1=Alessandra |title=Kofi Cockburn signs undrafted free agent contract with Utah Jazz |url=https://foxillinois.com/sports/fighting-illini/kofi-cockburn-signs-undrafted-free-agent-contract-with-utah-jazz |access-date=24 June 2023 |work=Fox Illinois |date=24 June 2022}} His contract wasn't picked up by the Jazz. On 16 November 2022, Cockburn signed with the [[Niigata Albirex BB|Niigata Albirex]] of the Japanese [[B. League]].{{cite web |title=コフィ・コーバーン選手 (Kofi Cockburn) 契約締結のお知らせ |url=https://www.albirex.com/news/detail/id=20598 |website=新潟アルビレックスBB |access-date=4 December 2024 |date=16 November 2022}} He averaged 19 points and 12.3 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=コフィ・コーバーンが新潟を退団…Bリーグで鮮烈プロデビュー飾り韓国移籍 |url=https://basketballking.jp/news/japan/b1/20230630/440040.html |website=バスケットボールキング |access-date=4 December 2024 |date=30 June 2023}} On 20 June 2023, Cockburn signed with the [[Seoul Samsung Thunders]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] (KBL).{{cite web |title=프로농구 삼성, 키 210㎝ 빅맨 외국인 선수 코번 영입 |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20230620068600007 |website=연합뉴스 |access-date=4 December 2024 |date=20 June 2023}} In May 2024, Cockburn re-signed with the Seoul Samsung Thunders.{{cite web |title=워니 등 외국선수 6명, 프로농구 각 구단과 재계약…라건아는? |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20240531130500007 |website=연합뉴스 |access-date=4 December 2024 |date=31 May 2024}} On 19 May 2025, Cockburn signed with the [[Hiroshima Dragonflies]] of the Japanese B.League.{{cite web |title=#23 コフィ・コーバーン選手 契約合意（新規）のお知らせ |url=https://hiroshimadragonflies.com/news/detail/id=20829 |website=広島ドラゴンフライズ |access-date=28 May 2025 |date=19 May 2025}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===Domestic leagues=== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size:100%; text-align:right;" !
